subject: Pilot kickoff: Atlantech — scope, success metrics, owners and next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Nadia Gomez <nadia.gomez@atlantech.com>, Marcus Lee <mlee@atlantech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot kickoff: Atlantech — scope, success metrics, owners and next steps

Hi Nadia / Marcus —

Thanks again for the productive discovery earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we schedule the formal kickoff: please see the bullets below and holler if anything looks off.

Key pain points you shared:
- High rate of false positives in intent classification for support triage (~18% FP right now).
- Latency spikes during peak hours causing slower agent routing.
- Cost per API call is unpredictable across current models and infra.

Primary goals for the pilot (30 days):
1) Improve triage precision (reduce FP from ~18% -> target <= 10%).
2) Maintain 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for the production-like load (sample QPS provided).
3) Prove cost per resolved intent at or below $0.004/token equivalent with Redwood batching + prefix caching.

Proposed pilot scope and deliverables:
- Dataset: 5k anonymized support transcripts (you mentioned SOC2 controls permit tagged subsets).
- Model: open-checkpoint LLM (we'll provide Redwood-calibrated quantized variant).
- Evaluations: prompt suite of 150 test cases (accuracy + hallucination checks) and rolling quality evaluation every 7 days.
- Observability: per-route latency and token-cost dashboard; weekly quality readout.

Owners and points of contact:
- Customer lead: Nadia Gomez (Atlantech product) — data & stakeholder signoffs.
- Customer infra/engineer: Marcus Lee — data transport/egress and environment access.
- Redwood lead: Olga Petrov — program management, coordination, and billing questions.
- Redwood PM: Marissa Cole — evaluation matrix, prompt set design, and quality gates.
- Implementation SME: Priyom Das — infra onboarding and sample deployment.

Timeline (tentative):
- Week 0 (this week): sign PoC charter and confirm data subset + access method.
- Week 1: data ingest + access verification; Redwood provides initial prompt/eval scaffold.
- Week 2: model deploy + run initial evals; first quality readout.
- Week 3: tuning and integration; final acceptance tests.
- Week 4: results summary and recommended production path.

Access/IR requirements we need from Atlantech this week:
- A representative sample (5k rows) of anonymized transcripts; CSV or S3 link.
- Network: a short-lived S3 role or secure pre-signed URLs for Redwood engineering.
- Security: confirmation of required redaction and SOC2 point of contact (we'll share an evidence packet).

Attachments included: redwood-poc-checklist.pdf (pilot checklist) and a simple sample prompt matrix in the Drive link below.

HubSpot deal link: https://hubspot.com/deal/7891
Drive doc: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cAtlantech-PoC-Plan

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Nadia: confirm the 5k sample can be shared this week (or provide ETA).
2) Marcus: confirm S3 access or alternative data transfer by Thu 21 Aug.
3) Atlantech legal: if you need a minimal PoC MSA, flag now — we can run a short-term exhibit.

If there's agreement, I'll slot a 30–45 minute kickoff for Friday and loop in the Redwood infra team for the handoff.

Thanks — speak soon.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-poc-checklist.pdf (pdf)]

Subject: Re: Pilot kickoff: Atlantech — scope, success metrics, owners and next steps

Hi Olga — thanks for the thorough summary. This matches our notes. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

1) Data: we can provide a 5k anonymized sample by EOD Thursday (21 Aug). We'll redact PII and provide a data dictionary. Marcus, can you confirm export timeline?

2) Metric tweak: for latency we want to measure 95th percentile on the combined routing flow (including our gateway) — would Redwood's latency dashboard ingest a synthetic routing hop so we get realistic numbers? If not, are there latency probes we can run alongside?

3) Legal: short PoC addendum sounds fine. I'll ask legal to review a 1-page exhibit — legal@atlantech.com has been CC'd.

4) Pricing/Capacity: once we run the initial eval, we may ask for an idea of committed capacity pricing if this scales — can you include a “indicative” cost delta for a 100k/month inference volume in the pilot materials? This is for internal planning only.

Approve next steps — please schedule the kickoff Fri 22 Aug 10:00–10:45 PT if that works for Redwood.

Thanks,
Nadia Gomez
Head of Product, Atlantech
